reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC5082-3-2.note: Re-read 2026-10-17 against the Section 6.1 sentence "This specification mandates setting and verifying TTL=255 of those as well as the main protocol packets." after the IPv4 receive proofs moved to match-scoped nft counters. Setting is unchanged: TestGTSMTransmittedICMPErrorCarriesTTL255 fails on packet[8]!=255 and the ICMPv6 twin on packet[7]!=255, over the route applyHopLimitRoutes installs, and the withdraw negatives bind the 255 to that route. Verifying, IPv4: TestGTSMDropsADangerousQuotedICMPError waits on the quoted-destination term's counter (bounded by captureWait), then fails when IcmpMsg InType3 rises, when any term other than exactly that one matched, or when TCPMinTTLDrop moved; Observed in an arm64 guest on kernel 7.2.9: Drop turned to Accept in peerTerms leaves the term matching and the message delivered, and the test goes red at the InType3 assertion. TestGTSMDeliversAQuotedICMPErrorAtTTL255 is a real negative: the same message at TTL 255 must raise InType3 by one and match no term, and with Accept plus the TTL match removed from peerTerms it was observed red at assertNoTermMatched, naming the quoted-destination term. rulePackets now fails a rule with no counter, so a vanished counter cannot read as no match. Verifying, IPv6: TestGTSMMinHopCountDropsALowHopLimitICMPv6Error fails when TCPMinTTLDrop does not rise, unchanged.

RFC5082-3-3.note: Independent post-lint judgment after reading the full RFC and actual socket boundary. RFC 5082 Section 3: 'On some architectures, the TTL of control plane originated traffic is under some configurations decremented in the forwarding plane. The TTL of GTSM-enabled sessions MUST NOT be decremented.' TestGTSMConfiguredEgressDoesNotDecrement configures RealDialer.OutTTL=255 and observes both SYN and exact data payload at the adjacent veth in a separate namespace. Every captured sender packet must carry TTL exactly 255. newTCPEgress creates two network namespaces, addresses the MTU-1500 veth and checks the route's egress link, so local delivery cannot substitute for the claimed path. Its promoted-field Veth literal retains Name, MTU, PeerName and PeerNamespace. receive/receiveFrame now return errors that the calling test makes fatal; IP total length, IP/TCP header bounds, peer link, bounded frame count, socket timeout and owned packet clone still guard the observer. Actual producer network.go::DialContext sets IP_TTL before the SYN through ttl_linux.go::setIPTTL; Linux's local-output path emits the captured packets. A TTL-setting omission or decrement to 254 fails the exact on-wire assertion. The owner's single-positive local-output scope is retained: there is no legitimate negative input for this invariant, and normal transit forwarding decrement is not the prohibited local-output behavior. This does not invent IPv6, ICMP or transit proof for this IPv4 carrier. Reviewed parent's job-network-wire-observers-privileged-cdc8e23e.log lines 43-46: this unit PASS, package PASS, no skip. Parent reports native Linux -race and only the test executable elevated via -exec 'sudo -n' within fixture-created private namespaces. Earlier pre-body privilege/restore failure proves nothing. Existing native setIPTTL-panic discrimination must be renewed for the changed unit; this audit neither executed nor claims that red.

RFC5082-3-4.note: Re-read 2026-10-17 against Section 3: "MUST NOT drop (as part of GTSM processing) packets classified as Trusted or Unknown." Trusted: TestGTSMFloorDeliversATrustedPacket fails if the packet at the floor is not received, unchanged. Unknown: TestGTSMNoFloorDeliversAnUnknownPacket is unchanged; TestGTSMDeliversAnICMPErrorNoSessionClaims, with the filter published, injects three unclaimed ICMP errors at TTL 1 and fails unless IcmpMsg InType3 rises by exactly one and no term's counter moved (a rule with no counter fails rather than reading zero). The test no longer proves the chain evaluated the message, an assertion the owner approved losing on 2026-10-17 because a match-scoped counter cannot see a non-match; that does not weaken this MUST NOT, whose observable is delivery, and TestGTSMDropsADangerousQuotedICMPError proves the same chain sees type-3 messages on the same path. With the 0x45 version/IHL match removed from quotedIPv4HeaderGuard, the options case was observed red in an arm64 guest on kernel 7.2.9 (InType3 did not rise), while the other two cases stayed green.
